name: sma_crossover_banknifty_5s
author: adapted from AI_Quant
thesis: This strategy targets short-term momentum in liquid Indian instruments. It exploits the inefficiency that aligned moving averages (MA10 > MA29 > MA100) indicate a strong intraday trend (bullish momentum)【18†L17-L24】. This exists because institutional flows often drive extended moves after the open, and many traders miss multi-timeframe signals. The pattern persists due to friction (trading costs) and the difficulty of front-running large players.
mechanism: Consolidation periods accumulate resting orders above resistance and below support. A breakout triggers these resting orders as stop-losses and breakout entries fire simultaneously. The resulting order flow imbalance overwhelms the resting liquidity, and market makers widen spreads in the breakout direction, accelerating the move.

conditions: close > sma_10 AND sma_10 > sma_29 AND sma_29 > sma_100

weaknesses: Underperforms in choppy or range-bound markets (no clear trend)
Exposure to sudden reversals or gaps (no overnight holdings but intra-day reversals)
Potential crowding risk from other moving-average traders
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to BANKNIFTY index.
